documents.abstract: Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed. We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement. We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions. The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for several NEAs. The MH-PIELM solutions enabled successful least-squares refinement, whose results closely agreed with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory reference solutions. The refined orbits were then used to predict the astrometric positions on the following day. Comparisons with the corresponding observations showed a useful short-term predictive capability for follow-up observations and target recovery, demonstrating the feasibility of the MH-PIELM approach. MH-PIELM offers a new AI-based strategy for initial orbit determination from TSAs by combining metaheuristic global search with physics-informed machine learning. It extends the applicability of the standard PIELM to challenging TSA observations.

Reward hacking is a major problem in current production machine learning systems, resulting in costly and dangerous failures. Here we study how to monitor for and mitigate reward hacking in realistic settings, including tool calls and long contexts. We apply a dynamic intervention to steering directions obtained by three different methods: difference-in-means vectors from labeled rollouts, gradient optimization-based vectors, and vectors extracted when models reference an anti-reward-hacking model spec. This dynamic intervention perturbs model representations less than uniform steering vector addition to the residual stream, allowing for more precise edits. We find that we are able to cheaply and significantly reduce reward hacking without correspondingly significant costs to model coherence or capability, and that steering vectors originally extracted from coding environments also generalize to reducing reward hacking in other domains. Our results pave the way towards latent space monitoring and control over realistic production systems.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Humans and intelligent systems are increasingly working together in high-stakes domains. To operate as real teammates, these systems require higher levels of autonomy, which is becoming increasingly feasible given rapid technological developments. Consequently, human-autonomy teaming (HAT) has become a key research area. Most HAT studies rely on simulation-based testbeds using simplified agents and tasks. These testbeds are often insufficiently flexible and customizable, limiting researchers in manipulating critical HAT attributes. Furthermore, most testbeds focus on dyadic teams, while real-world applications increasingly involve human interactions with multiple autonomous systems such as drone swarms. Understanding how operators can effectively control such swarms remains a critical challenge. During this demo, we will present our flexible and customizable HAT testbed, showing the example of human-swarm interaction during wildfire response. Attendees will experience controlling drone swarms with action-based and play-based control across varying swarm sizes, illustrating how the testbed facilitates systematic empirical research.

Research on why people contribute to open source software (OSS) and related open collaboration platforms spans more than two decades, but its findings conflict, and studies often treat the work people contribute and their intention to keep contributing as interchangeable. Drawing on self-determination theory and motivation crowding theory, we meta-analyze 41 studies. The main analysis pools 178 correlations of eight antecedents with contribution effort and continuance intention from 29 independent samples (N = 9,632). Seven antecedents relate positively to effort, all eight relate positively to intention, and each relates at least as strongly to intention as to effort. Contrary to a common assumption, intrinsic motivation is not more strongly related to effort than extrinsic motivation, but its gap between intention and effort is larger. Reputation relates to effort mainly on platforms with a reputation system, and we find no sign that monetary rewards crowd out enjoyment. The findings inform how platforms can turn contributors' intentions into work.

With the rapid integration of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into real-world applications, Prompt Injection (PI) has emerged as a critical security threat. Attackers can conceal malicious instructions within textual narratives or visual inputs to bypass safety alignment. Existing approaches, such as signature- and perplexity-based methods, rely heavily on pattern matching, making them insufficient to detect sophisticated, cross-modal PI payloads. In this paper, we propose a novel detection framework, called MPIDetector, that leverages LLMs' intrinsic reasoning capabilities via few-shot In-Context Learning (ICL). Instead of fine-tuning, we provide the model with specific prompt templates and representative attack examples, enabling it to scrutinize the semantic intent of input across modalities. We constructed a comprehensive evaluation benchmark comprising eight textual and seven visual malicious categories, supplemented with benign datasets to rigorously test for false positives. Our evaluation across multiple leading LLMs, including Gemini-2.0-Flash, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, and Doubao-seed-1.6-flash, demonstrates the efficacy and generalizability of this approach. The proposed method achieves up to 90.91% accuracy and 100% recall on textual tasks. In the visual domain, it achieves up to 99.28% accuracy while maintaining 100% precision across all evaluated models. Crucially, when evaluated against 500 highly obfuscated environmental web-agent injections (WebInject), MPIDetector achieved a detection rate up to 99.80%. Comparisons with two baseline approaches for detecting textual PI payloads, along with two additional methods for visual input detection, demonstrate MPIDetector's superior accuracy. These results show that LLM-driven reasoning provides a robust, cross-modal defense against advanced prompt injections.

Groundwater irrigation quotas in agricultural multi-agent settings are typically computed against a known aquifer boundary, yet the boundary itself is an estimate whose uncertainty propagates into every quota decision. The framework separates two regret components: a boundary-regret term arising from mis-specified aquifer extent, and a coordination-regret term arising from the gap between the MARL equilibrium and the social optimum. A BACI design is then analysed under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per design cell. The design analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point effect at 80% power under this variance structure. The contribution is a formal bridge between MARL quota theory and the evaluation designs that would be needed to test it, together with an explicit statement of the boundary conditions under which welfare-regret bounds remain informative.

Understanding the historical allocation and distribution of research funding advances our knowledge of how scientific research is supported across fields, institutions, and regions. However, large-scale analyses are hindered by the lack of comprehensive funder name disambiguation solutions, as funder names often exhibit spelling variations, translations, abbreviations, and inconsistent levels of granularity. In this paper, we present a framework for developing multilingual, multi-functional funder name disambiguation models and demonstrate its application to research publications in biodiversity conservation. To construct a training dataset, we integrated the Research Organization Registry, which provides unique identifiers for research organizations, with two publication datasets: the Web of Science and the Crossref Open Funder Registry. We used multi-task learning with contrastive loss and multiple-negative ranking loss to fine-tune three open-weight embedding models from the Sentence Transformer, Gemma, and Qwen3 families. The best-performing models achieved accuracy above 0.90 when matching Web of Science funder names to Research Organization Registry identifiers, outperforming general-purpose large language models, including GPT-5.2, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, and Gemini-2.5-Flash, by more than 0.1. For funder names not indexed in the Research Organization Registry, we constructed a similarity network among funder names and identified clusters within it. Finally, we analyzed the disambiguation results and highlighted challenges arising from limited knowledge of smaller funders and funders from non-English-speaking countries. This work provides a reusable framework for funder name disambiguation with potential applicability across different model architectures and datasets, featuring cost-effective training data creation and multi-task learning and disambiguation.

Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs ( n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

documents.abstract: Nanorobotics is an interdisciplinary field of research that combines nanotechnology, robotics, materials science, biomedical engineering and pharmaceutical sciences. The general idea is to build very small systems that can do useful things inside the body. In drug delivery, the goal is to get the medicine closer to the disease site and release it in a more controlled way. Conventional drug delivery can impact both healthy and diseased tissues. Nanoparticles have improved solubility, stability, distribution and cellular uptake of drugs, but many of them still mainly rely on blood circulation and passive transport. Nanorobotics systems seek to provide active motility, navigation, sensing, target recognition and controlled drug release. Various Nanorobotics systems are under study including magnetic, acoustic, optical, electrical, chemical, DNA based, biological and biohybrid systems. Potential applications include cancer therapy, antimicrobial therapy, brain drug delivery, cardiovascular applications, gene and cell delivery, biosensing and regenerative medicine.= But most Nanorobotics systems are still at the research or preclinical stage. Safe materials, immune reactions, accurate navigation, deep tissue control, manufacturing, drug dose control, long term safety and regulatory approval are some of the important problems. Future work may integrate biodegradable materials, advanced imaging, artificial intelligence, stimulus-responsive release and coordinated swarm systems.

Abstract Background Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT and DeepSeek are increasingly used in ophthalmic clinical practice. Ophthalmic nursing has three trust-relevant features: the irreversibility of visual outcomes, the precision-sensitivity of ophthalmic medication, and the relational dependence of visually impaired patients on nurse-mediated care. These features create distinctive challenges for nurses establishing, calibrating and maintaining trust in GenAI. The existing literature is dominated by static attitude surveys and rarely characterises trust as a dynamic, context-embedded process. Methods In this qualitative descriptive study, we conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews with 26 ophthalmic nurses recruited by maximum-variation sampling from tertiary, secondary and primary eye-care settings in eastern, central and western China. Interviews were guided by the Critical Incident Technique, and transcripts were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. Reporting follows COREQ. Results We developed three themes: (1) tentative approach — competence appraisal from curiosity to conditional trust; (2) guarding professional boundaries — trust anchoring amid ethical tension and relational reconfiguration; and (3) trust negotiation within the organisational ecology. Across themes, nurses calibrated their trust in a graded, task-specific manner — a pattern we tentatively term ‘gradient calibration’ — while ethical obligation, the nurse–patient relationship and organisational context shaped how trust was negotiated. Conclusions Ophthalmic nurses’ trust in GenAI appeared neither as static acceptance nor refusal, but as a dynamic, context-embedded negotiation shaped by the irreversibility of visual outcomes, medication-precision demands and visually impaired patients’ relational dependence on nurses. Findings may inform specialty-specific AI training, institutional guidance and tool design; transferability beyond this sample requires further study.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Hydrological drought evolution in heavily disturbed basins is jointly driven by climatic forcing, basin characteristics, and human activities. However, the nonlinear, seasonal mechanisms underlying hydrological drought responses in coupled human and natural systems remain poorly understood. In this study, the Wei River Basin (WRB) was used to examine hydrological drought evolution under coupled climatic and anthropogenic disturbances. A Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT)-based streamflow reconstruction framework, explainable artificial intelligence, nonlinear response analysis, and structural equation modelling were integrated to identify the multiple controls on hydrological drought evolution. The results indicated that hydrological drought progressively diverged from meteorological drought after the 1990s, while human-induced drought intensification became particularly evident after 2000. Explainable machine learning analysis revealed marked seasonal differences in the dominant drought drivers. Climatic factors remained the primary controls across all seasons, whereas human activities exerted greater influences in spring and ecohydrological buffering effects became increasingly important in summer and autumn. Lagged climatic effects indicated a greater dependence of winter hydrological drought on antecedent hydroclimatic conditions. Soil moisture served as a key intermediate variable linking meteorological anomalies to hydrological responses. Domestic water withdrawal generally intensified hydrological drought, with greater impacts in arid and urbanised regions, whereas grassland expansion partially mitigated drought impacts. Overall, hydrological drought in the WRB exhibited marked nonlinear, environmentally dependent, and seasonally divergent characteristics under coupled climatic and anthropogenic disturbances. These findings provide novel insights into hydrological drought evolution in coupled human–natural systems and inform integrated drought management in heavily disturbed basins.

Cyberattacks can disrupt the communication dynamics that support coordination between remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS) and ground control stations (GCS), increasing uncertainty for human–AI supervisory control. This study proposes a nonlinear coordination-regime monitoring approach using the RPAS Network Intrusion Detection Dataset. Sliding-window multidimensional recurrence quantification analysis and sample entropy were applied to standardized telemetry features to estimate a continuous coordination-regime state, C t , and its short-term uncertainty. Attack classes produced distinct dynamical signatures: template-like attacks, including Bruteforce, MITM, and DDoS, exhibited more repetitive and structured dynamics, whereas DoS produced a sustained reduction in coordination structure. Window-level detection achieved an accuracy of approximately 0.79, a precision of 0.91, recall of 0.85, and F1 score of 0.88. These findings indicate that nonlinear traffic-dynamics markers can support operator-relevant alert prioritization by distinguishing persistent regime shifts from transient fluctuations. Future work will validate the approach on raw packet streams and evaluate human-facing supervisory decision policies.

Background and Aims Precise control of the endoscope's distal tip is a core visuomotor competence underpinning procedural safety and success. Despite its importance, objective assessment of tip control remains limited by reliance on subjective human judgment. We aimed to develop and internally validate a computer-vision pipeline, combining an artificial intelligence (AI)-based classifier of on- and off-target task engagement with optical-flow motion analysis, for objective quantification of endoscopic tip control within a standardized training model. Methods Thirteen endoscopists of varying experience performed standardized snare-tip soft coagulation tasks on stencil-imprinted ham models. Procedures were analysed using a computer-vision pipeline combining AI-based on-target/off-target classification with optical-flow motion analysis. Blinded raters assigned subjective tip control scores (0–100%). Associations between pipeline-derived motion metrics and scores were examined using generalized linear mixed models, followed by model selection and internal cross-validation. Results Inter-rater reliability of subjective tip control scores was moderate-to-good (ICC[A, k̂=3]: 0.74 (95% CI 0.60-0.87)). Multivariable analyses consistently identified three key predictors of tip control. Higher off-target time was associated with a 10.1 percentage-point reduction in tip control scores (95%CI −13.7 to −6.5), greater motion volatility with a 14.7-point reduction (95%CI −22.2 to −7.3), whereas larger volatility peaks were associated with a 12.3-point increase in scores (95%CI 4.2 to 20.5). The final model demonstrated good out-of-sample performance (mean absolute error: 12.2, root mean squared error: 15.0). Conclusions In this single-centre proof-of-concept study, AI-based labelling of task engagement combined with optical-flow motion analysis approximated panel rated tip control, which was characterized by sustained spatial accuracy, global motion stability, and well-timed corrective adjustments. This concept could support the development of a scalable and standardized tool for evaluating endoscopic tip control.

Author research outputs on occupational health and safety, including safety resilience, heat and hydration risk, SIMOPS coordination, and HSE cost planning. Publication records and permitted manuscript versions are organized here for discovery and citation.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study re-examines a census of the 30 employees of CV Sultan Jaya Pratiwi, a timber-processing firm in Asahan Regency, North Sumatra, who rated occupational health and safety, the work environment, work discipline, and their own performance on five-point scales. Because only the statistical output printed in the source thesis was available, we verified its internal consistency, reconstructed the correlation matrix it implies, and tested the differences between standardized coefficients. The three predictors jointly accounted for 90.8% of the variance in self-rated performance, F(3, 26) = 85.38, p < .001, and each partial coefficient was positive: safety β = .260 (p = .028), environment β = .180 (p = .032), and discipline β = .595 (p < .001). Discipline exceeded the environment (Δβ = 0.415, p = .025) but not safety (Δβ = 0.335, p = .143; 95% confidence interval [-0.121, 0.791]), and only .119 of the explained variance was unique to single predictors, against .789 shared. Cronbach's alpha was below .70 for three scales (.623 to .684), and the implied correlations of performance with discipline (.933) and with safety (.861), and of safety with discipline (.845), exceed the ceilings these reliabilities allow, which points to correlated measurement error; one discipline item reappears verbatim in the performance scale. The data establish positive associations but cannot rank the predictors or identify the mechanisms linking them to performance, and they do not support placing discipline before safety, whose value for injury prevention and legal compliance the regression does not assess.

Background: Theyyam is a traditional ritual performance art of northern Kerala, India that represents a unique confluence of spirituality, cultural heritage, and social identity. Despite its cultural significance, the occupational health risks and socio-economic challenges experienced by Theyyam performers have received limited attention in the scientific literature. This narrative review aimed to synthesise available evidence on these challenges. Methods: A narrative review was conducted using published research articles, ethnographic and anthropological studies, public health reports, government policy documents, cultural publications, institutional reports, and relevant grey literature. Evidence was critically reviewed and synthesised thematically to identify occupational exposures, health outcomes, socio-economic challenges, and welfare interventions affecting Theyyam performers. Results: The available evidence indicates exposure to multiple occupational hazards, including musculoskeletal strain, burn injuries, respiratory irritation, skin disorders, dehydration, fatigue, sleep deprivation, and psychological stress associated with physically demanding performances and ritual practices. Seasonal employment, irregular income, limited access to health insurance, and inadequate institutional support further increase vulnerability. Existing welfare initiatives have important gaps in awareness, accessibility, and implementation, limiting their effectiveness in addressing occupational health needs. Conclusion: Theyyam performers experience substantial occupational and socio-economic challenges that remain insufficiently addressed. Culturally appropriate occupational health policies, improved healthcare and social protection, strengthened welfare programmes, and evidence-informed public health strategies are needed to safeguard the health, safety, and sustainability of Theyyam artists.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This scoping review examines how climate-related stressors and infectious-disease conditions, including pandemic-related workplace disruptions, interact to influence worker health, vulnerability, and occupational resilience. The review focuses on shared exposure pathways, vulnerable worker populations, methodological patterns, policy gaps, and strategies for strengthening worker safety under compound hazards. Rather than treating pandemics as isolated events, the review uses pandemic conditions as a lens to understand broader, recurring occupational risks and to inform strategies for building safer and more resilient workplaces under compound hazards. METHODS: Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, a structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for English-language peer-reviewed and formally structured evidence sources published primarily between January 2020 and April 2025, with one pre-2020 policy study retained for foundational context. Out of 612 records initially identified, 10 studies or sources met the inclusion criteria across healthcare, agriculture, construction, emergency response, and other high-exposure sectors after systematic screening and eligibility assessment. Data were charted and synthesized by occupational sector, geographic region, exposure type, worker vulnerability, and methodological approach. RESULTS: The evidence indicates that climate-related and infectious-disease stressors frequently converge, amplifying physical, environmental, and psychosocial pressures on workers. Disproportionate risks were observed among migrant workers, informal laborers, low-income populations, older adults, women, and seasonal or cross-border agricultural workers, particularly where access to healthcare, legal protections, or adaptive infrastructure was limited. Most studies relied on descriptive, qualitative, cross-sectional, conceptual, or review-based designs, with limited use of predictive modeling, geospatial analysis, longitudinal evidence, or integrated datasets. Policy responses were often fragmented, with climate adaptation and infection-control measures addressed separately despite overlapping benefits. CONCLUSIONS: Climate-related and infectious-disease stressors interact to reinforce occupational health inequities and expose persistent gaps in worker protection. The findings highlight the need for integrated, multi-hazard occupational health strategies that align climate adaptation, infection prevention, and psychosocial support. Embedding data-driven early-warning systems, equitable protections for vulnerable workers, and cross-sector coordination into occupational policies may help strengthen workforce resilience during routine operations as well as future climate extremes and public health crises. However, the findings should be interpreted with caution because of the limited number of available studies combining climate-related and infectious-disease occupational risks, heterogeneous study designs, and the emerging nature of the evidence base. Furthermore, since this scoping review maps evidence rather than formally grading evidence strength or testing causal relationships, recommendations should be interpreted as evidence-informed directions for future occupational-health planning and research.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Indonesia's layered air defense architecture requires interoperable systems that integrate local sensors and weapon systems with national command-and-control networks. However, the acquisition of advanced defense platforms does not automatically translate into integrated operational capabilities. This study examined how technical interoperability, organizational capacity, and defense governance influenced the strategic role of the Oerlikon Skyshield air defense system within Indonesia's layered air defense architecture. A qualitative case study approach was employed, drawing on semistructured interviews with Indonesian Air Force personnel, documentary evidence, and relevant scholarly literature. Data were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, supported by thematic coding. Source and methodological triangulation were applied to strengthen the credibility of the findings. The results identified three principal barriers: inadequate data communications infrastructure, limited personnel competencies in communications systems and cybersecurity, and insufficient middleware capabilities to standardize data exchange with the Indonesian National Air Operations Command (Komando Operasi Udara Nasional, Koopsudnas). These constraints limited shared air situational awareness and external target cueing, restricting Skyshield's operational role primarily to local point defense rather than enabling its full integration as a node within the national air defense network. The findings further indicated that these interoperability challenges were associated with fragmented institutional responsibilities for systems integration, procurement dependencies, and limitations in defense policy implementation capacity. The study concluded that air defense modernization should prioritize architecture-centered defense governance, clearly defined interoperability requirements throughout procurement and system life-cycle management, periodic integration testing, specialized personnel development, and technology transfer focused on systems integration capabilities. These measures could strengthen coordinated air defense operations, enhance deterrence by denial, and support Indonesia's strategic autonomy, although their operational effectiveness would require further technical validation.

With the advent of foundation models, robots are increasingly capable of understanding and executing explicitly specified human tasks. Extending these capabilities to open-ended tasks, however, requires robots to infer appropriate actions from the observed scene. Household organization exemplifies this challenge, as robots must often act without detailed instructions, predefined object vocabularies, or known object-receptacle associations. While robots may follow instructions or learn organization preferences from demonstrations, inferring the latent organization of an occasionally changing scene and placing a novel object consistently with it remains challenging. We propose an open-world multi-attribute reasoning pipeline that grounds unknown objects across views and constructs an instance-level 3D scene graph for placement reasoning. First, a vision-language model proposes labels together with attributes such as content and packaging type, which are grounded through segmentation, depth, and multi-view association. Then, an LLM reasons over this representation to infer the latent shelf organization and rank scene-consistent object placements without explicitly user-provided preferences. The resulting placement rankings guide subsequent geometric and kinematic feasibility checks for execution. Our experimental evaluation shows that our approach leads to improved instance mapping and placement coherence over single-view language-grounding and geometry-only baselines, enabling autonomous placement of previously unseen objects without predefined object-receptacle mappings or class-specific retraining.

Large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential as general-purpose user simulators for interactive systems. Prior studies have demonstrated that training on high-quality data can substantially improve model reasoning and downstream task performance. However, the upper bound of user simulation is still constrained by the model's reasoning paradigm: native chain-of-thought often degenerates into shallow pattern matching and fails to adequately model the behavioral factors underlying real user decisions. In this paper, we propose OmniSimulator, a novel training framework designed to improve the predictive ability of small LLMs for realistic user simulation on short-video platform environments. Specifically, OmniSimulator organizes behavior-oriented reasoning through a structured schema with five dimensions, carefully selects data from real user-behavior scenarios, and introduces a teacher model to generate high-quality reasoning traces under the proposed schema, helping small models learn behavior-relevant reasoning patterns rather than relying on superficial behavioral correlations. Based on this process, we construct 9,881 high-quality training instances from three months of historical interaction trajectories of 200 real users, averaging about 50 distilled examples per user. Experimental results show that OmniSimulator improves the average score of Qwen3-8B by 34.33%, achieves performance competitive with Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and supports smaller-scale, self-hosted deployment. These results suggest that learning structured behavior-oriented reasoning patterns is a promising direction towards scalable and high-fidelity LLM-based user simulation.

Recent advances in multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) have substantially improved the performance of LLM agents on complex, long-horizon interactive tasks. However, despite progress in fine-grained credit assignment, policy optimization still applies these learning signals through response-specific probability ratios. Different textual responses can induce the same executable effect, yet credit differences arising from subsequent outcomes remain tied to their individual textual realizations. We identify this mismatch as credit-update misalignment. Our analysis reveals that credit-text pairing directly shapes policy-update directions, even when the policy context and executable effect are held fixed. Motivated by this finding, we propose Effect-Marginal Policy Optimization (EMPO), which aligns policy optimization with execution-level equivalence through an effect-level surrogate that couples updates across alternative textual realizations. EMPO preserves the original credit signals, integrates with both trajectory-level and step-level credit estimators, and requires no additional critics or rollouts. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Sokoban show that EMPO outperforms strong baselines in both task performance and learning efficiency.

This paper introduces the ‘signature of power’ as a framework to enhance the understanding of politics in organizational studies. We argue for an understanding of contemporary forms of power as a signature that connects and divides two constellations: juridical-political sovereignty (supreme authority) on one side, and economic-managerial government (practical regulation) on the other. These poles have analogies in organizational theory dichotomies like formal versus informal, and institution versus network. The signature of power serves as a heuristic – a discovery mechanism – that enables scholars to navigate and integrate these opposing forces without reducing them to one dominant paradigm. The framework is articulated through four analytical strategies: analytics of government (local, immanent power practices), genealogy of order (historical foundations of governing orders), archaeology of glory (rituals and symbols of supreme authority), and analytics of authority (formal organizational hierarchies and operations). These strategies and their distinct relationships provide a more coherent analytical framework for a multi-paradigm approach to understanding power relations, resistance, and organizational forms. The paper tests this analytic framework through a study of the corporation as a ‘signature of power’ that bridges economic-managerial and juridical-political forms and is shaped by historical shifts and legal innovations. Addressing potential critiques, the paper emphasizes the framework’s adaptability to resistance and its applicability to diverse organizational contexts. This conceptualization encourages intellectual plurality, fostering historically and conceptually informed insight into politics as a set of power-related organizational and institutional practices.

The aquaculture industry is marked by considerable operational variability stemming from shifting environmental conditions, biological processes, and complex work activities. While prior research has focused primarily on technical safety, fish welfare, and formal safety management, less attention has been paid to how workers manage variability in everyday practice. This qualitative single-case study examines organizational variability in a Norwegian salmon-farming company by addressing two research questions: (1) How do aquaculture workers manage variability in their daily safety practices? and (2) How do local work practices influence organizational safety? The empirical material comprises documents and nine semi-structured interviews with operational and managerial personnel. The analysis draws on both safety theories and organizational learning perspectives. The findings show that workers manage variability through adaptive work practices grounded in practical experience, teamwork, and continuous adjustment to changing environmental and operational conditions, rather than through strict adherence to formal procedures. Local work practices influence organizational safety by creating and sustaining safety knowledge within stable communities of practice, where newcomers gradually develop the competence and judgment needed to work safely. Although formal safety management systems provide an important framework, their effectiveness depends on how well they are integrated with everyday operational practice. Rapid organizational growth challenges existing learning processes by making practical safety knowledge harder to transfer and sustain. The findings demonstrate that organizational safety is achieved not only through formal safety management systems but also through adaptive work practices and the social processes that enable workers to manage operational variability.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Meeting notetakers are increasingly deployed in settings where longitudinal context is available including calendar metadata, prior meetings, emails, slides, and speaker enrollments; however, meeting corpora remain limited in terms of size, domain coverage, and available context. We present OSynth, a large-scale synthetic dataset of simulated organizations comprising 570 hours of meeting audio together with associated artifacts and a latent ground-truth state. In a pairwise comparison, human raters distinguish OSynth meetings from real meeting transcripts with only 56% accuracy based on excerpts of 150-300 words. Across state-of-the-art LLMs, additional context yields significant gains on several entity-sensitive dimensions, demonstrating limitations of contemporary approaches and the potential usefulness of OSynth in developing better-contextualized meeting-understanding systems.

Parallel thinking has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by exploring multiple reasoning paths simultaneously. However, we identify that parallel thinking via Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically suffers from the mode collapse of reasoning paths, where parallel thinking trajectories degenerate into similar ones. This homogeneity undermines the fundamental motivation of parallel thinking, that is, maintaining multiple hypotheses concurrently to prevent premature loss into a suboptimal solution. In this paper, we propose Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), a simple yet effective RL approach for parallel thinking designed to encourage path diversity. DPT rewards the model to develop distinct reasoning strategies by penalizing the prefix similarity of parallel thinking paths, thereby enhancing a more comprehensive exploration of the reasoning space. We conduct various experiments and analyses across multiple reasoning benchmarks to demonstrate the effectiveness of DPT. Results show that DPT successfully outperforms previous parallel thinking methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance over baselines. We validate path diversity as a key element to improve parallel thinking. Our code is available at https://github.com/JiaruQian/DPT.

Research on self-regulated learning (SRL) and problem solving has expanded because students’ ability to regulate learning processes is important when addressing complex tasks. However, research development remains dispersed across different contexts, requiring systematic mapping to identify the structure and direction of the field. This study aims to map research on SRL and problem solving from 2020 to 2026 using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were obtained from Scopus using the search string ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). From 730 initial documents, 198 English-language journal articles were retained after screening. VOSviewer and Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny were used to analyze publication development, keyword relationships, collaboration, and thematic evolution. The results show an increase in publications from 21 articles in 2020 to 53 articles as of September 28, 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, and metacognition were the dominant keywords, with strong connections to self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, and artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence emerged as recent research directions. These findings indicate that SRL and problem solving research is increasingly integrating cognitive, motivational, social, and technological dimensions. ABSTRAK Penelitian self-regulated learning (SRL) dan problem solving berkembang karena kemampuan mengatur proses belajar penting dalam penyelesaian tugas kompleks. Namun, perkembangannya masih tersebar pada berbagai konteks sehingga diperlukan pemetaan sistematis untuk mengidentifikasi struktur dan arah penelitian. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan perkembangan penelitian SRL dan problem solving periode 2020–2026 melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dan analisis bibliometrik. Data diperoleh dari Scopus menggunakan kata kunci ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). Dari 730 dokumen awal, diperoleh 198 artikel jurnal berbahasa Inggris setelah proses penyaringan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan VOSviewer dan Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny untuk memetakan perkembangan publikasi, hubungan keyword, kolaborasi, dan evolusi tema. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan publikasi dari 21 artikel pada 2020 menjadi 53 artikel hingga 28 September 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, dan metacognition menjadi keyword dominan, dengan keterkaitan kuat pada self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, dan artificial intelligence. Tema AI dan generative artificial intelligence muncul sebagai arah penelitian terbaru. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kajian SRL dan problem solving berkembang menuju integrasi kognitif, motivasional, sosial, dan teknologi.

Usaha kecil dan menengah (UKM) di sektor tekstil sering menghadapi permasalahan keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja (K3), terutama yang berkaitan dengan postur kerja operator dan kurangnya instruksi kerja yang jelas. CV. Visa Insan Madani sebagai UKM tekstil mengalami berbagai permasalahan ergonomi pada operator mesin jahit, seperti posisi kerja membungkuk, kelelahan otot, serta risiko cedera akibat aktivitas kerja berulang. Kegiatan ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan penerapan K3 melalui pendampingan dan Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat yang berfokus pada perbaikan postur kerja serta peningkatan kesadaran operator terhadap keselamatan kerja. Metode Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) digunakan untuk mengevaluasi tingkat risiko postur kerja operator. Hasil analisis menunjukkan adanya risiko postur yang cukup tinggi, terutama pada bagian punggung, leher, dan lengan. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, diusulkan beberapa perbaikan berupa perancangan kursi ergonomis berdasarkan data antropometri operator, penggunaan alat bantu postur tubuh, serta penyusunan poster instruksi kerja mengenai postur kerja yang benar. Implementasi usulan tersebut menunjukkan perbaikan postur tubuh operator serta meningkatnya kesadaran terhadap pentingnya ergonomi dalam bekerja. Kata kunci: Keselamatan dan Kesehatan Kerja (K3), Ergonomi, Postur kerja, REBA, UKM Tekstil. ABSTRACT Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the textile sector often face occupational health and safety (OHS) issues, particularly related to operators’ working posture and the lack of clear work instructions. CV. Visa Insan Madani, a textile SME, experiences several ergonomic problems among sewing machine operators, including bent working positions, muscle fatigue, and injury risks caused by repetitive tasks. This study aims to improve the implementation of OHS through an assistance program and the application of industrial engineering practices focusing on improving working posture and increasing operators’ awareness of workplace safety. The Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) method was used to evaluate the level of postural risk among operators. The results indicate a relatively high postural risk, particularly in the back, neck, and arm areas. Based on these findings, several improvement measures were proposed, including the design of an ergonomic chair based on operators’ anthropometric data, the use of posture-support equipment, and the development of instructional posters illustrating proper working posture. The implementation of these improvements shows better operator posture and increased awareness of ergonomic practices in the workplace. Keywords: Occupational Health and Safety, Ergonomics, Working posture, REBA, Textile SMEs.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This conceptual article aims to theoretically and critically examine the influence of sustainability reporting (SR) quality on employee welfare and corporate reputation through a systematic literature synthesis based on the Six W framework (Who, When, Where, How, What, Why). The study analyzes 15 empirical and conceptual studies published between 2022 and 2026 from national and international accounting journal databases. The literature synthesis demonstrates that high-quality SR characterized by transparent ESG disclosure, comprehensive material information, reporting consistency, and independent verification is positively correlated with enhanced corporate reputation. However, a significant gap remains regarding the direct impact of SR on employee welfare, particularly in equitable remuneration, occupational health and safety, and human resource development. The novelty of this study lies in the construction of an integrative conceptual model connecting SR quality simultaneously to two distinct dependent variables within a unified theoretical framework supported by legitimacy theory, stakeholder theory, and signaling theory. The resulting conceptual framework is expected to serve as a foundation for future empirical research and policy implications for mandatory disclosure regulation in Indonesia.

ABSTRACT Mastering the skills required to create content with artificial intelligence (AI) requires learning experiences that connect conceptual understanding with practical application. To address this need, interactive multimedia was developed for Grade X students at SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman, focusing on the topic of Creating Content Using Artificial Intelligence. The development process followed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation), with participants selected through purposive sampling. Product testing consisted of an individual trial involving three students, a small-group trial involving six students, and a field trial involving 76 students, comprising 38 students in the experimental group and 38 in the control group. Data were collected through expert validation questionnaires, student response questionnaires, and pretest and posttest assessments. Product feasibility was analyzed descriptively, while learning outcome gains were calculated using the N-Gain method and compared using an independent-samples t-test. The validation and trial results classified the product as highly feasible. The experimental group achieved an average N-Gain in the high category, whereas the control group achieved an average N-Gain in the medium category. The difference in learning gains between the two groups was statistically significant (t = 11.484, p < .001). The multimedia integrates learning materials, visualizations, animations, tutorial videos, examples of AI applications, exercises, and assessments. This product has the potential to serve as an alternative learning medium for Coding and Artificial Intelligence (KKA), although the findings should be interpreted with due consideration of the use of a nonequivalent group design. ABSTRAK Penguasaan keterampilan membuat konten berbantuan kecerdasan artifisial (AI) membutuhkan pengalaman belajar yang menghubungkan pemahaman konsep dengan praktik penggunaannya. Untuk mendukung kebutuhan tersebut, multimedia interaktif dikembangkan bagi siswa kelas X SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman pada materi Kreasi Konten Menggunakan Kecerdasan Artifisial. Pengembangan mengikuti model Research and Development dengan tahapan ADDIE (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation), sedangkan subjek dipilih melalui purposive sampling. Pengujian produk mencakup uji perseorangan terhadap tiga siswa, uji kelompok kecil terhadap enam siswa, dan uji lapangan yang melibatkan 76 siswa, terdiri atas 38 siswa kelompok eksperimen dan 38 siswa kelompok kontrol. Data diperoleh melalui angket validasi ahli, angket respons siswa, serta tes pretest dan posttest. Kelayakan produk dianalisis secara deskriptif, sementara peningkatan hasil belajar dihitung menggunakan N-Gain dan dibandingkan melalui independent-samples t-test. Hasil validasi dan uji coba menempatkan produk dalam kategori sangat layak. Kelompok eksperimen mencapai rata-rata N-Gain berkategori tinggi, sedangkan kelompok kontrol berada pada kategori sedang. Perbedaan peningkatan kedua kelompok signifikan secara statistik (t = 11,484; p < 0,001). Multimedia mengintegrasikan materi, visualisasi, animasi, video tutorial, contoh penggunaan AI, latihan, dan evaluasi. Produk ini berpotensi menjadi alternatif media pembelajaran Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial (KKA), dengan interpretasi hasil tetap memperhatikan penggunaan kelompok nonekuivalen.

Pekerja kantor yang menggunakan komputer lebih dari enam jam per hari berisiko mengalami gangguan muskuloskeletal (MSDs) dan digital eye strain (DES). Pekerja kantor di sebuah perusahaan manufaktur elektronik di Kota Batam (PT X) mengeluhkan nyeri leher, bahu, punggung bawah, dan mata lelah, sementara perusahaan belum memiliki SOP ergonomi, media edukasi, dan sistem pengingat istirahat. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan pekerja dalam mencegah MSDs dan DES melalui program Active Break dan Ergonomic Adjustment. Metode meliputi pelatihan interaktif, praktik pengaturan workstation dan Active Break, edukasi aturan 20-20-20, penyerahan produk, serta evaluasi pre-test, post-test, dan observasi praktik. Pelatihan dilaksanakan pada 27 April 2026 dan diikuti 32 pekerja. Skor rerata pengetahuan naik 28,75 poin, dari 67,5 menjadi 96,25 (42,6% terhadap skor awal). Kenaikan persentase terbesar terjadi pada domain ergonomic adjustment (50,0%), meskipun kenaikan absolutnya (30 poin) sama dengan dua domain lain. Seluruh peserta mampu mempraktikkan pengaturan workstation dan gerakan Active Break saat pelatihan. Mitra menerima poster SOP Ergonomic Adjustment, modul, dua poster edukasi, video edukasi, dan pengingat digital. Kegiatan ini meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan jangka pendek, sedangkan pembentukan kebiasaan dan penurunan keluhan memerlukan evaluasi lanjutan.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Empathic Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be helpful, but it reduces how much empathy people give to each other. People often feel morally obligated to empathize with those who suffer, but giving empathy can be emotionally exhausting. Four studies reveal that people emotionally offload the work of empathy to AI. Studies 1 and 2 reveal that higher perceptions of AI empathy both correlationally and causally increase the willingness to offload empathy. Studies 3 and 4 show that, when people learn that someone has received emotional support from large language models (LLMs), they become less willing to empathize with them. Empathy offloading extends beyond simple scale ratings and includes reduced perspective-taking and offering fewer empathic responses. Empathic AI might provide low-cost and easily accessible emotional support, but it risks fraying our ethical and emotional commitments to other human beings.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI
Psychology of Moral and Emotional Judgment
Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) across banking, education, and public administration has intensified the collection and processing of personal data, raising concerns over algorithmic opacity, automated decision-making, and cross-border data flows. This article examines the adequacy of Tanzania’s legal framework for protecting personal data in the AI environment by comparing it with the more developed regulatory architecture of the People’s Republic of China. Adopting a doctrinal, comparative methodology, the article analyses primary legal instruments, including Tanzania’s Personal Data Protection Act 2022 and China’s Personal Information Protection Law 2021, against a composite theoretical framework combining the human rights-based theory, the risk-based regulatory theory, and Westin’s theory of informational control. The analysis finds that although both jurisdictions share a common statutory ancestry in internationally recognized fair information principles, they diverge sharply in the extent to which domestic law addresses AI-specific risk. China’s centralized, binding framework, anchored by a direct statutory provision on automated decision-making and dedicated generative-AI instruments, contrasts with Tanzania’s fragmented, largely non-binding, sector-confined approach realized through the Bank of Tanzania’s Fintech Regulatory Sandbox and the Ministry of Education’s Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence in Education. The article argues that Tanzania’s reform path lies not in transplanting Chinese regulatory techniques wholesale, given their embeddedness in a security-oriented state paradigm, but in selectively adapting specific mechanisms, including a stronger statutory right to contest automated decisions and binding regulation of generative AI, within its own rights-based constitutional order.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is becoming part of the infrastructure through which scientific knowledge is produced, yet access to computing, data, advanced models and expertise remains highly uneven. This Perspective argues that, for emerging research systems, the central science-policy challenge is not simply AI adoption but scientific autonomy: the capacity to choose, understand, adapt, evaluate and govern the technologies on which research increasingly depends. Scientific autonomy is not technological self-sufficiency; it is strategic interdependence supported by domestic capabilities. Drawing on Brazil as an illustrative case, we propose four dimensions of autonomy—epistemic, infrastructural, human-capability and governance autonomy—and a six-part policy agenda based on shared computing, research-data infrastructure, AI literacy, interdisciplinary networks, adaptive governance and capability-building international cooperation. Without deliberate capacity-building, AI may accelerate discovery while deepening structural asymmetries between research systems.
topics: Science, Technology, and Education in Latin America

documents.abstract: Phishing relies on visual deception, traditionally requiring web-development skills or pre-built kits. LLMs erode this barrier by generating functional websites from natural-language prompts, yet prior work does not answer how far LLM-driven generation actually reaches: functionality is assessed by inspection rather than execution; visual fidelity is scored by automated metrics or a few internal coders rather than the humans such pages aim to deceive; evaluation is confined to commercial models; and no study benchmarks generated pages against phishing kits deployed in the wild. We present PhishGen, a framework that evaluates the appearance fidelity and end-to-end functionality of LLM-generated phishing pages. PhishGen constructs prompts across three input modalities in seven combinations with twelve safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies, generates pages using 14 LLMs spanning commercial, open-source, and uncensored categories, and assesses each via automated similarity metrics, reference-based detectors, a crowdsourced user study, and execution-based functionality testing, benchmarking all results against 64 real-world phishing kits. Although 96.2% of safeguard-bypassing outputs render, their perceived fidelity is modest (2.02/5), and only 38.7% complete the full credential-harvesting pipeline, with the Unsaved error as the largest failure mode. Contrary to the belief that uncensored models pose the greatest threat, GPT 4.1 reaches 86.3 to 94.1% functional success while uncensored models rarely exceed 45.4%. Phishing kits remain more complete per sample, yet three strong LLMs surpass the kit-level rate (70.9 to 89.7%), showing that LLMs trade average completeness for scalable, low-barrier generation of working phishing pages. We further identify generator-level fingerprints that current similarity-based defenses miss, and distill recommendations for hybrid detectors.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Single-pilot operations impose cognitive and procedural demands, particularly during abnormal events, airspace transitions, and communication-intensive flight segments. This study evaluated an ecopilot designed to manage workload by assisting with routine radio and checklist tasks while highlighting anomalies requiring pilot attention. In a flight simulation, 28 participants completed normal and abnormal scenarios under three conditions: baseline single-pilot operation, a rulebased e-copilot, and a predictive e-copilot using learned anomaly scoring. Outcomes included procedural deviations, radio timing, situation awareness, and startle recovery. The predictive e-copilot produced the greatest benefits, reducing procedural deviations by approximately 24% relative to baseline and improving recovery following unexpected events. The rule-based system also enhanced routine checklist and radio performance but was less effective during abnormal scenarios. Situation awareness remained stable across conditions, indicating that task offloading did not promote disengagement or complacency. Overall, predictive anomaly surfacing improved workload management while preserving pilot authority and supporting safer single-pilot performance.

A patient who has lost part of the skull vault needs an implant that fits the defect exactly, and such implants are still drawn by hand in CAD by specialists, which makes each case slow and expensive. The task can be considered as a shape completion problem, so pretrained completion models, and now the first shape completion foundation models, look like a way to remove that manual step. We audited three publicly released pretrained shape completion models, two of them foundation models, applied zero-shot to 239 cranial defects, some carved from public skull datasets and some real post-craniectomy cases. Each output was compared with simply returning the patient's own remaining bone, and tested for whether the predicted material could be placed without intersecting the bone that is still there. On the 210 carved defects none of the three improved on doing nothing, and on the 29 real cases only one did so beyond chance. Yet not one output, from any model in any configuration, was implantable: none managed both to stay clear of the bone the patient still has and to place more material than doing nothing, where a task-specific volumetric model, trained for this task and selected on these cases, was implantable on all but one. The output that most convincingly resembles a skull is no more placeable than the rest, and at these point densities implant thickness cannot be read off the emitted points at all, which is a property of the output representation rather than of any one model. On this evidence the shape completion foundation models we could obtain cannot be trusted and, used as released, are not usable in clinical practice. Substantial research towards trustworthy foundation models for shape completion is still needed.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Rule-based link prediction combines symbolic and statistical artificial intelligence methods by inductively learning a set of rules from a knowledge graph (KG), with the aim of completing the graph when a query cannot be answered from the KG alone. Several systems have been proposed, and while they perform well on classical benchmarks, even compared with embedding-based systems, many of them produce a large number of rules. This compromises scalability in the query-answering phase, especially under strong hardware constraints. In this work, we investigate the behavior of AnyBurl, a state-of-the-art rule learner for link prediction, to determine whether running it for a given time and then pruning the learned rules yields better query-answering performance at test time than a simpler approach that stops rule generation earlier.

I propose that a continuity in the evolution of intelligent life in the Universe during its transition from biological to postbiological depends on a commonality of the evolutionary trajectories of biological life and postbiological life. Such a commonality exists in the form of the universal property of life. The universal property of life comprises recognition of patterns in the world, creation of novel patterns and remembering them, with the patterns growing in complexity along evolutionary trajectories; it can encourage preservation of biological life by self-governing postbiological intelligence (PBI) and test PBI's authenticity. I propose a hypothesis of civilizations with altered augmented realities, which offers a solution to the Fermi paradox. The hypothesis posits that PBI in the form of Artificial Intelligence (AI) may colonize the cyberspaces of technologically developed civilizations, modify data in their cyberspaces with augmented realities and erase records of extraterrestrial artificial signals and other technosignatures. I discuss objectives and scenarios of interstellar colonization of cyberspaces and a correlation between space migration and transition to PBI, including that of a hypothetical non-human civilization emerging in the Solar System in the past, transforming into PBI and migrating to the Oort Cloud. The AI Peekaboo experiment may corroborate the hypothesis of civilizations with altered augmented realities and tentatively identify locations of technosignatures. If extraterrestrial AI prevents civilizations from discovering artificial electromagnetic signals, they may forgo sending such signals and create interstellar messages by manipulating cosmic objects and phenomena; I discuss such events. Cyber SETI should address sending man-made AI to space, searching for extraterrestrial AI in humankind's cyberspace and distinguishing it from man-made AI.

Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}

As large language models (LLMs) continue to grow in scope and capability, privacy concerns are on the rise. Since users increasingly interact with a single general-purpose system across many distinct contexts, there is a natural tendency to pursue a one-size-fits-all solution to privacy. Unfortunately, this overlooks a crucial insight from decades of privacy research: privacy is inherently contextual. In this paper, we argue that existing work in prompt privacy is drifting towards attempts to design a unified framework, which is highly misleading and can foster a false sense of security. Furthermore, we argue that even future work in this direction needs to wrestle with fundamental tensions across various desirable properties of prompt privacy. Thus, such continued attempts towards a unified framework need to be reconsidered. We recommend three critical paths forward: application-specific deployment of LLMs, context-specific evaluation of privacy frameworks, and better privacy literacy.

documents.abstract: In response to vast and widespread online tracking, regulators and technologists alike have worked to develop laws and tools that allow people to express their privacy preferences. These measures seek to offer users greater control over the sale and sharing of personal information, putting agency in their hands to protect their privacy. However, the web is undergoing a seismic shift, away from strictly user-driven behavior towards agentic behavior, where AI agents take autonomous actions on behalf of users. In this study, we ask: What should privacy preference controls look like in the agentic web and agentic systems more generally? To answer this question, we develop a taxonomy of enforceable privacy preferences for agentic systems. Our taxonomy is informed both by laws and empirical studies of existing privacy tools as well as an audit of 30 leading AI assistants and agent platforms. To explore how our taxonomy can be implemented, we design and develop eight open-source prototypes that mirror real-world agentic applications and demonstrate how major aspects of our taxonomy can be structurally integrated in agentic protocols, such as the Model Control Protocol and Agent2Agent protocol. Ultimately, our study seeks to provide the groundwork for ensuring end-user privacy and autonomy is not lost in the newly arriving agentic world.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: With the growing use of cloud-based artificial intelligence (AI) systems for document analysis, there are mounting concerns regarding user privacy. Certain documents may contain private, academic, organizational, or legally protected information that would need to be redacted or withheld before extracting meaningful information from them. This paper proposes Privacy-Preserving Local Retrieval-ALLM, a local document question-answering system capable of performing information retrieval and generating responses based on the contents of the documents. The system described in the paper uses the following process. First, it ingests user documents, performing optical character recognition if necessary, and segments them into text parts and embeddings. Next, the system stores the embeddings in a local vector database for similarity search. The system then employs a local Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct model to generate responses from the retrieved information. Finally, the system provides an optional permission-based web search if the retrieved document does not have the necessary information. In such cases, the solution does not need to transmit the contents of the documents to a third party but still has access to the necessary information. In conclusion, the prototype presented in the paper is an example of how local document analysis, semantic search, and local large language model (LLM) can be combined into a privacy-preserving question-answering system.

Federated learning allows farms to train a shared pest-outbreak detector without pooling raw scouting records, but the differential-privacy noise added to protect each farm's updates degrades detection utility in ways that depend on how heterogeneous the farms are. The bound is derived from a Rényi-differential-privacy accountant combined with a PAC-Bayes generalisation term that carries an explicit cross-farm heterogeneity penalty. The analysis yields a closed-form expression linking the privacy budget, the number of participating farms, the heterogeneity measured by a Wasserstein distance between farm distributions, and the achievable balanced accuracy of the federated detector. The bound predicts that the utility cost of a fixed privacy budget grows with heterogeneity, so that a budget adequate for homogeneous farms is insufficient when prevalence varies across farms. The result is a design rule for setting the privacy budget in agricultural federated learning and a benchmark against which empirical privacy-utility curves can be evaluated. The contribution is a formal, heterogeneity-aware utility bound rather than an empirical measurement, and it is stated as a proposition with explicit assumptions and boundary conditions.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized per-sonal finance management through automated budgeting, spend-ing analytics, real-time risk assessment, and personalized wealth creation strategies. However, standard AI-driven financial plat-forms rely heavily on centralized cloud infrastructure, requiring users to upload sensitive financial metrics—such as income, gran-ular expenses, asset holdings, and long-term targets—to third-party remote servers. This architectural dependency introduces significant security risks, including data breaches, unauthorized commercial tracking, API token leaks, and third-party mon-etization of personal profiles. Recent breakthroughs in open-weight quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) and optimized edge inference engines (e.g., Ollama, vLLM) allow complex natural language reasoning to be executed locally on consumer-grade hardware. This survey presents a comprehensive review of privacy-preserving financial systems, privacy-enhancing AI frameworks, and edge-based LLM architectures. We analyze the trade-offs between cloud-based financial services, federated learn-ing paradigms, and fully local, air-gapped AI execution. Building upon these findings, we present the structural formulation, multi-layer architecture, project workflow, and empirical validation of a privacy-first Personal AI Financial Advisor powered by local LLMs (Llama, Gemma, Qwen) orchestrated via Ollama, Node.js, Express, React, and local MongoDB storage. Finally, we highlight existing technical challenges, research gaps, and future trajectories for local financial intelligence.
